claude.performance_metric: announced sale of 400+ funeral homes + 100+ cemeteries (2001); homes fell to ~2,500, footprint 20→8 countries
claude.rationale: gap_45=0 because §2 shows T4 (retained family-name products) and T5 (cluster-pooled operations) moved together coherently — the cluster process operated across the retained-name products for years (§4 P4). gap_56=0 because T5 re-engineering (pooled hearses/embalming/personnel) was structurally aligned with T6 (staff shared across the cluster), not a mismatch. p4_pathway=0 because §4 states no discrete product-process integration failure was documented. p5_pathway=0 because §4 records no specifically documented process-organization fracture ([UNVERIFIED]); by contrast the documented failure was t2_model incompatibility — the acquisition/death-rate value logic inverted (§3, §4).

gemini.performance_metric: stock dropped by more than 40 percent; announced plans to sell over 400 funeral homes plus more than 100 cemeteries
gemini.rationale: The dossier explicitly states that the cluster process operated across the retained-name products for years, indicating no structural mismatch at closing (gap_45=0) and no subsequent product-process disruption (p4_pathway=0). Furthermore, there is no documented evidence of a process-organization structural gap at closing (gap_56=0) or any subsequent fracture between operations and people/culture (p5_pathway=0).

grok.performance_metric: stock fell >40% in 1999; divested >400 homes + >100 cemeteries by 2001 (homes to ~2,500)
grok.rationale: Section 2 T4 states names/brands preserved whole while T5 states processes re-engineered to cluster model (gap_45=1); T5 re-engineered while T6 only partial/pooled (gap_56=1). Section 4 explicitly codes P4 and P5 as none documented (both 0) but T2-model incompatibility as PRESENT due to inverted acquisition economics and declining death rate.
